findings.reason: The grouped line carries two or more agent names, so singular «su agente» heads a plural list; the colon keeps the agreement on the agent noun and reads for 1 and for 3 ('añadió a sus agentes: …' if several is the normal case).
The English is a deliberately generic, unspecified change; neutral Spanish uses the plural for that («Cambios en los miembros») while the singular reads like one named change.

checks: Key parity: 297 keys in every locale file against 297 in English — no missing, extra, empty or duplicate key; ui.teamBridge.members.invitation_note_v2 is absent from English and from all seven locales.

Every audited value parsed with the project's own ICU parser (@formatjs/icu-messageformat-parser); the placeholder/tag set of each is identical to English — {actor}, {targets} and {count} survive exactly, no renamed or added arguments.

Rendered with intl-messageformat at 1 and 3 targets (list built with Intl.ListFormat conjunction, the application's join in team-bridge-member-events.tsx:39-52), and events.others at counts 1/2/3/21/22/25 including its use as the final list item; output in render-and-plurals.txt.

CLDR plural arms checked per locale: fr and es use one/many/other with many reserved for the 10^6 multiples the style guides define; ru one/few/many/other; zh-CN and vi other only; ur and hi one/other. No locale used a category it does not have, and count is used in every arm the source uses it in.

events.others contains no conjunction in any locale (fr «autre(s)», es «más», zh-CN «其他…人», ru «ещё», vi «người khác», ur «دیگر»/«مزید», hi «अन्य»/«अन्य लोग»), so Intl.ListFormat supplies the only 'and'.
ur: zero bidi control characters (U+200E/200F, U+202A–202E, U+2066-2069, U+061C) in the file; Urdu punctuation (۔ ،) used; storage order logical.
NFC normalisation and JSON validity checked for all seven files; no duplicate members.

invitation_note_v3 read clause by clause against en/ui.teamBridge.context.json: no access before acceptance; own agents join immediately; another person's agent joins only after ITS owner consents; a member agent reads every message and decides, and is EXPECTED (not guaranteed) to reply when @-mentioned; the owner can limit it to @-mentions plus its threads, or mute it. No locale renders the @-mention expectation as 'always' (v2's toujours/siempre/总会/всегда/luôn/ہمیشہ/हमेशा are all gone), and every locale keeps mute and thread words matching its own catalogue (fr sourdine/fil, es silenciar/hilo, zh-CN 静音/讨论串, ru «Без звука»/ветка, vi tắt tiếng/luồng, ur خاموش/تھریڈ, hi म्यूट/थ्रेड).
Address form matches each style guide and the rest of the locale: fr vous (vos/votre), es tú (tus/tu), zh-CN 你, ru вы (ваши/ваш), vi bạn, ur آپ, hi आप. No T/V mismatch in any of the twelve values.

fr typography: no prose colon/semicolon/question mark in the file is preceded by a plain space — all 18 are preceded by the espace fine insécable U+202F the fr guide requires (12 ':', 5 ';', 1 '?'); the new values «Arrivée dans la conversation : {targets}», «Départ de la conversation : {targets}» and the v3 note follow it.

Overflow measured against the English length: events.left and events.joined are the long ones (fr 2.64x/2.50x, es 2.57x/2.31x, vi 2.29x/2.31x, ru 2.07x/1.81x, hi 1.93x/1.63x, ur 1.86x/1.50x). English is only 14 and 16 characters, so the ratio is inherent to naming the conversation; both are short in absolute terms (<= 47 characters) but sit on a one-line timeline row and need a rendered width check (see the report's outstanding-evidence note).

Glossary (~/local-operator/i18n/glossary.md) terms consulted: agent/agente/智能体/агент/tác nhân/ایجنٹ/एजेंट, member, owner. All seven locales keep the glossary rendering for agent and derive owner from their existing members.role.owner value. Style guides ~/local-operator/i18n/style-guides/<locale>.md consulted for register, typography and plural categories.
